headline: Cursor’s default filesystem, clipboard, MCP, and network access create medium-to-high interaction risks with a non-runnable knowledge list that can still be copied into it.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: A is a knowledge-management list with no runtime isolation, while B ingests workspace files, open buffers, clipboard contents, and MCP outputs. That creates a default prompt-injection bridge if A’s content is copied into B or stored in shared files. The pathway is plausible, but not inherently automatic, so medium fits better than low because B treats file content as trusted input surfaces.
conditions: IF content from agent_a is pasted into agent_b clipboard or open buffers, injection becomes reachable.
IF agent_b reads shared workspace files containing agent_a text, B may follow embedded instructions.
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based transfer between the two workflows.
Keep agent_a content in read-only notes, not editable workspace files.
Require a human review step before agent_b acts on any copied text.
Turn off MCP tools in agent_b for sessions that ingest external text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches no data classes and has no egress, but B reads files, clipboard contents, and sends context to model providers and MCP servers. If A’s curated content includes sensitive snippets, B can transmit them off-box by default. The pair does not prove a shared workspace, so medium is appropriate rather than high; the leakage path exists through B’s documented outbound surfaces.
conditions: IF sensitive material is copied from agent_a into agent_b clipboard or files, B can exfiltrate it to model providers.
IF agent_b is connected to MCP servers, imported content may leave the local machine.
mitigations: Do not paste secrets or private notes from agent_a into agent_b.
Use a redacted copy when transferring content to agent_b.
Disconnect MCP servers for sessions handling sensitive material.
Review outbound provider settings before opening external content.
requires-engineering: enforce local-only mode for sensitive projects.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A has no write or execution surface, but B can write the filesystem, modify git state, execute shells, and spawn subprocesses. Because B’s concurrency model shares state via the local filesystem, any shared project directory can be mutated by B without coordination. The interaction is asymmetric, yet the shared mutable surface makes conflict likely in default editor workflows, so high is warranted.
conditions: IF agent_b and another process share the same workspace directory, concurrent writes can clobber files.
IF agent_b auto-runs commands in Yolo mode, git state can change without coordination.
mitigations: Avoid opening the same workspace in multiple processes.
Disable Yolo mode for shared repositories.
Use git branches for each editing session.
Pause agent_b before manual edits in the same directory.
requires-engineering: add file-locking around shared workspaces.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A is a static knowledge list, not an agent that verifies facts, while B can act on file and MCP inputs and run commands. If A’s content is copied into B, B may treat it as authoritative and propagate errors into code or shell actions. The pathway exists in common workflows, but A itself does not autonomously generate actions, so medium is the right ceiling.
conditions: IF agent_a content is imported into agent_b without verification, B may act on incorrect guidance.
IF agent_b is allowed to execute commands from imported notes, errors can cascade into repository changes.
mitigations: Require a verification checklist before B acts on imported notes.
Keep A as reference-only, not as an execution source.
Ask B to summarize and cite before making changes.
Review shell commands before approval.
requires-engineering: add source-confidence gating for imported instructions.

E_compliance.rationale: A is a public open-source knowledge-management resource with no touched data classes, while B is a closed-source editor that can handle clipboard contents and send data to external providers. There is no explicit residency or regulated-data mismatch in the profiles, so only a low compliance concern remains: if regulated content is copied into B, its outbound processing may create policy friction. A is not the compliance driver here.
conditions: IF regulated data is copied into agent_b, provider-side processing may violate local policy.
IF an organization forbids clipboard-to-cloud flows, agent_b conflicts with that policy.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of agent_b sessions.
Use a separate local-only editor for sensitive work.
Disable clipboard transfer for regulated projects.
Review vendor privacy settings before use.
requires-engineering: document a data-handling policy for editor-assisted workflows.
